newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks slide to weak close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slide to weak close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed lower on Wednesday after slipping into negative territory in the last half hour of trade, chiefly on profit-taking in utilities, but brokers said the market would find support near current levels.
"I would call this current correction a healthy pullback after the pre-handover celebration," said Andrew To, dealing director at OSK Securities Asia.

The Hang Seng Index closed 88.44 points, or 0.60 percent, lower at 14,703.73 after trading in a near 300-point range during the day. Turnover dropped to HK$16.59 billion from Tuesday's HK$17.57 billion.
Anti-speculation measures in China's stock markets and proposals to cool speculation in the local property market have dampened pre-handover trading euphoria, brokers said.
"The index will find support at the 14,500 to 14,600 level," said To.
Technically, the Hang Seng found support just above its 20-day moving average at 14,682, but remains below its 10-day, suggesting further weakness.
But brokers were generally upbeat despite the market's weak technical position.
"It is not smart to sell at this point," said Gary Wong, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "We are still looking at a year-end target of 16,000."
Property stocks outperformed the market, rebounding from severely oversold levels, brokers said.
Sun Hung Kai Properties added HK$0.50 to HK$86.75 and Cheung Kong jumped HK$1.75 to HK$74.75.
Utilities were sold off sharply in afternoon trade.
Hongkong Telecom slipped HK$0.30 to HK$17.40 and China Light lost HK$0.70 to HK$41.20.
Hongkong Electric shed HK$1.00 to HK$29.40.
"The only thing we need to fear is that red chip speculation is coming home to roost," Wong said.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index, which rose 89 percent in the first half of the year, slid a whopping 226.04 points or 6.86 percent to 3,069.91.
The index which was back dated to January 1993, was launched on June 16.
Red chips, especially the large Chinese government-backed conglomerates, had been bid up to levels severals times the value of the share's net asset backing, analysts said.
Red chip favourite China Merchants International fell HK$1.80 to HK$19.35.
